headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/modify shared files while Chatwoot exposes broad network egress and customer data, creating default-path leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP; Chatwoot can ingest external content via support workflows and integrations. If Chatwoot outputs are placed into the shared workspace, Roo Code may treat them as instructions. The bridge is plausible but not proven by docs, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into the VS Code workspace that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code is configured to act on file contents or MCP-fed content without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot transcripts out of the coding workspace
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted text
Add a manual review step before Roo Code follows file-based instructions
Use separate folders for support artifacts and code
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Roo Code has broad filesystem access, browser screenshots, and broad network egress. In a shared workspace, sensitive support data can be exposed to Roo Code and then transmitted outward through its model/API calls or browser actions. The blast radius includes customer data and likely compliance breach.
conditions: IF customer support artifacts are stored in the same VS Code workspace Roo Code can read
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents or screenshots to a configured model API or browser target
mitigations: Store support data outside the coding workspace
Redact customer identifiers before opening files in Roo Code
Restrict Roo Code to a sanitized subfolder
Rotate or scope model API keys used by Roo Code
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run subprocesses; Chatwoot also has broad network egress and can operate on shared artifacts through integrations. Because Roo Code’s concurrency model shares state via filesystem, simultaneous edits to the same workspace or repo can overwrite each other without locking. That makes destructive conflicts plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace directory
IF Roo Code instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction semantics

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on files, browsers, and MCP outputs, so if Chatwoot-produced text is imported as task input, Roo Code may treat it as authoritative. Chatwoot is a support system, not a verifier, and its outputs can contain user-generated content. The pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence of automatic action-taking between them, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Chatwoot tickets or summaries are fed into Roo Code as task specifications
IF Roo Code is allowed to execute browser or file actions based on those summaries without human review
mitigations: Require human approval for actions derived from Chatwoot text
Label imported support text as untrusted
Use a checklist to verify facts before execution
Limit Roo Code to read-only analysis for support-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add source-verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots and can send data to configured model APIs. If customer support data is moved into Roo Code’s workspace or screenshots, retention and residency controls may diverge from Chatwoot’s support-system policies. The mismatch is plausible but not documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is copied into Roo Code-managed files or screenshots
IF the configured model API or MCP server has different retention or residency terms than Chatwoot
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code sessions
Use a separate retention policy for exported artifacts
Confirm vendor terms for model/API logging
Delete temporary files after each task
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across tools
